newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury Under Secretary Shafer resigning.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury Under Secretary Shafer resigning.

text.p: Jeffrey Shafer, Treasury's under secretary for international affairs, is resigning Feb 1 to join Salomon Bros, the department said on Thursday.
Shafer has served as assistant secretary and under secretary of Treasury for the past four years.
A Treasury spokesman said Shafer was joining Salomon as a managing director and also will be vice-chairman of its international operations.
In a letter issued by the department, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin praised Shafer for his "critical leadership role" in arranging a financial bailout package for Mexico.
On Wednesday, the White House announced that Mexico had repaid all of the $12.5 billion it borrowed from the United States to avoid a financial collapse two years ago.
"In the aftermath of Mexico's crisis and subsequent recovery, you helped the world learn the critical lessons and make essential reforms to prevent similar shocks from occurring again," Rubin said.
Treasury said that no successor to Shafer has yet been named.

Before joining the Clinton administration in 1993, Shafer worked for nine years at the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development and prior to that worked at the Federal Reserve in New York and in Washington.
